text: It was Pauls afternoon to appear before the faculty of the Pittsburgh High School to account for his various misdemeanors, for he had been suspended a week before. <break time="0.8s" /> He entered the room smiling, and although his clothes were a trifle outgrown, there was something of the dandy about him, for he wore a red carnation in his buttonhole. <break time="0.8s" /> The faculty felt that this red flower was not at all suited to the contrite spirit that befitted a boy who had been sent home in disgrace. <break time="0.8s" /> When questioned by the principal, Paul stated, politely enough, that he wanted to come back to school, though this was a lie, for he found lying indispensable for overcoming friction. <break time="0.8s" /> His teachers were asked to state their charges against him, which they did with such rancor and aggrievedness as showed that this was not a usual case. <break time="0.8s" /> Disorder and impertinence were among the offenses named, yet each instructor felt that the real cause of the trouble lay in the boys hysterically defiant manner and his open contempt. <break time="0.8s" /> Paul stood through it all smiling, his pale lips parted over his white teeth, and he used his eyes in a conscious, theatrical way, peculiarly offensive in a boy. <break time="0.8s" /> Afterward the drawing master voiced the feeling of them all when he declared that there was something wrong about the fellow, something that none of them understood. <break time="0.8s" /> He had once seen Paul asleep at his desk, and he remembered with a shock how old and tired the boys white face had looked, as if something were haunting him.
